question: During artificial rupture of membranes (ARM), a house surgeon plans to insert the amnihook. Which of the following steps is ESSENTIAL to prevent cord prolapse immediately after membrane rupture?

answers.text: Apply fundal pressure simultaneously to push the presenting part deeper into the pelvis

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Fundal pressure during ARM is not standard practice and may dislodge the presenting part. The presenting part must be fixed at the pelvic brim by the assistant's hand at the abdomen.

answers.text: Confirm that the presenting part is engaged (or well-applied to the cervix) before rupturing membranes

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. If the presenting part is high or mobile, cord prolapse is a serious risk when membranes rupture and liquor rushes out. ARM should only be performed when the presenting part is well-applied.

answers.text: Perform ARM with the patient in the left lateral position to avoid aortocaval compression

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Lithotomy or semi-recumbent position is standard for ARM; the left lateral position is used for aortocaval relief in other situations but is not the primary requirement for safe ARM.

answers.text: Insert the amnihook only after placing a Foley catheter to decompress the bladder first

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Routine bladder catheterisation is not required before ARM. The indication for ARM is cervical dilatation of at least 2–3 cm with adequate descent, not bladder status.

overallFeedback.feedback: The critical safety check before ARM is engagement of the presenting part. A high head plus ruptured membranes allows the umbilical cord to slip alongside or below the presenting part — an obstetric emergency.
Correct. A well-engaged or applied presenting part is the primary safety check before ARM — an unengaged head with ruptured membranes creates the conditions for cord prolapse.
